context: A uni student interviews a retired judge at home
purpose: Teach: 公判/判事/ノーベル/飼育/曲線/半数/根底/療養

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間いただきありがとうございます。卒論のテーマで、元判事の方にお話を伺いたくて。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. For my thesis I wanted to interview a former judge.
lines.style: Polite, slightly nervous student greeting an elder authority figure with formal humility.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いやいや、退官してもう十年だよ。今は自宅療養しながら、のんびり庭の世話をしている身だ。
lines.en: Oh come now, I retired ten years ago. These days I convalesce at home and tend to the garden.
lines.style: Warm elderly chuckle, self-deprecating tone with gentle pride in his quiet life.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ご療養中にすみません。先生が担当された公判の中で、特に記憶に残る事件はありますか?
lines.en: Sorry to intrude during your recovery. Was there a trial you presided over that left a mark?
lines.style: Apologetic but eager, leaning forward with notebook open and pen ready.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうだな、ある冤罪事件だ。証拠の半数が捏造だと分かった瞬間、司法への信頼が根底から揺らいだよ。
lines.en: Well, one wrongful conviction case. The moment I learned half the evidence was fabricated, my faith in justice shook to its core.
lines.style: Heavy reflective sigh, voice lowering with the weight of decades of conscience.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 根底から、ですか……。判事という職業の重さを感じます。
lines.en: Shaken to the core, you say. I feel the gravity of being a judge.
lines.style: Quiet, awed murmur, momentarily forgetting his prepared questions.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 学者がノーベル賞を狙って研究するのとは違ってね、我々の判断は誤差の曲線がそのまま誰かの人生になるんだ。
lines.en: Unlike scholars chasing a Nobel Prize, for us judges the curve of error becomes someone's life directly.
lines.style: Measured philosophical tone, hands folded as if speaking to himself more than the student.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど……ペットを飼育するような無責任さは決して許されない、ということですね。
lines.en: I see. So you can never approach it with the careless attitude of someone raising a pet.
lines.style: Thoughtful student nodding slowly, trying to rephrase the elder's wisdom in his own words.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そう、そこに気づけたなら立派なものだ。君の論文、楽しみにしているよ。
lines.en: Yes, if you grasp that, you'll do fine. I'll look forward to reading your thesis.
lines.style: Soft approving smile audible in voice, encouraging tone of a mentor recognizing growth.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。今日のお話、本当に有意義でした。
lines.en: Thank you so much. Today's conversation was truly meaningful.
lines.style: Sincere closing bow in voice, genuinely moved beyond the academic exercise.
